recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit. No current FHIR source edit is recommended for FHIR-5917. Treat FHIR-5796 as related context rather than a decided related issue here because it also covered contained-resource versioning rules outside this seed's DELETE/meta.deleted scope.
issue_request: FHIR-5917 was a Published/Persuasive FHIR-core BaseResource change request asking the specification to state whether a server should ignore meta.deleted or return an error when a resource DELETE operation conflicts with a submitted meta.deleted value.
initial_application: The Jira comments say Meta.deleted was an editorial mistake and then state that Meta.deleted was gone. The matching source application is SVN revision 4609, preserved as git commit 612bb5891be2abc43dd06bacbdfcbf853aac0213, which deletes the Meta.deleted row from source/datatypes/meta.xml; that commit references task #5796 rather than FHIR-5917.
additional_context: FHIR-5796 is a same-period Published/Persuasive BaseResource issue whose resolution explicitly says SVN revision 4609 deleted meta.deleted and made contained-resource Meta rules. Current source/fhir.ini lists Meta as an active datatype and maps meta to the resource page. Current Meta source defines versionId, lastUpdated, source, profile, security, and tag, with no Meta.deleted element. Validly quoted Zulip and Confluence searches found no conflicting community record.
reconciliation: No source change was made. Because Meta.deleted is not a current exchange element, conformant current FHIR resources cannot create the conflict described by FHIR-5917; adding ignore/error guidance now would reintroduce obsolete terminology.

related_jiras.note: Its Published/Persuasive resolution identifies SVN revision 4609 as deleting meta.deleted, which is the source application that also satisfies FHIR-5917.
